verdicts.tldr: an unquoted attribute value runs through `<`, so a line of `<gno-button x=` makes each attempt read up to 2 KB, not one tag as the ADR says
verdicts.details: scanGnoTag returns at `<` only at attribute start (`case c == '<': return 0, false`). The unquoted-value loop stops only at whitespace or `>`, so in `<gno-button x=<gno-button x=...` the value `<gno-button` is consumed and the scan continues to maxButtonTagLen (2048). The ADR says the scanner stops at the next `<` outside a quoted value, so each attempt reads one tag (ADR lines 88-90); for this shape it does not. Cost stays linear but each attempt reads up to 2048 bytes instead of about 14. The same code is in #6297 and #6299. Fix: stop the unquoted-value loop at `<` as well (`&& src[i] != '<'`) and add this shape to BenchmarkButtonHostileLine.
verdicts.evidence: read utils.go:66-108: `case c == '<': return 0, false // the next tag` sits only in the attribute-start switch; the unquoted branch is `for i < len(src) && !util.IsSpace(src[i]) && src[i] != '>' { i++ }`; ext_buttons.go:39 `const maxButtonTagLen = 2048`; ADR:88-90 `stops at the bound and at the next `<` outside a quoted value, so each attempt reads one tag`. Timing not run (read-only judge).
verdicts.verify_by: read utils.go:66-115 and confirm `<` ends an attempt only at attribute start (line 71) and not inside an unquoted value (line 105); time parseButtonTag on strings.Repeat("<gno-button x=", 1000) against strings.Repeat(`<gno-button href="/r/x" `, 1000) and compare bytes read per attempt (2048 vs ~24)

verdicts.tldr: a label of only U+061C, U+2060 or U+180E renders a blank button, and entity decoding uses text rules, not attribute rules as the godoc says
verdicts.details: buttonLabel strips only isBidiOrZeroWidth (U+200B-200F, U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+FEFF) and unicode.IsControl, which covers Cc only. U+061C (a Bidi_Control mark), U+2060 and U+180E are Cf, so they survive and the `label == ""` gate at line 72 passes. The result is a button that shows no text. The godoc also says entities are decoded as HTML decodes attribute text, but html.UnescapeString runs with `const attribute = false`. So a legacy entity with no `;` followed by `=` (for example `&not=`) is decoded, where a browser would keep it as written. #15 and #16 report the same strip-set gap. Fix: in buttonLabel (not in the VM native), also drop unicode.Cf runes, and either decode with attribute rules or reword the godoc.
verdicts.evidence: read markdown.go:47-58 isBidiOrZeroWidth ranges (no 0x061C, 0x2060, 0x180E); ext_buttons.go:97-106 `case !unicode.IsControl(r): return r`; go1.25.9 src/html/escape.go:56-57 `func unescapeEntity(...)` / `const attribute = false`, line 142 `else if attribute && ... s[i] == '='`. verdicts.tldr: benchConvert ignores weburl.Parse's error, unlike every other caller in the package's tests
verdicts.details: Line 113 reads `gnourl, _ := weburl.Parse("https://gno.land/r/test")`. Every other call in the package's tests uses `gnourl, err :=` and checks err. The input is a constant, so in practice the user loses nothing; the benchmark just lacks the guard that would catch a parse regression. Fix: `gnourl, err := weburl.Parse(...); if err != nil { b.Fatal(err) }`.

verdicts.tldr: inside every button the link icon keeps a 0.2em right margin, because the realm-view link rule outranks the button's `margin: 0`
verdicts.details: The built main.css has `.c-realm-view a>.tooltip:last-of-type{margin-right:.2em}`, specificity (0,3,1), and `.c-realm-view .gno-button>.tooltip{...margin:0}`, specificity (0,3,0). The higher specificity wins whatever the source order, so the icon in a button sits 0.2em further from the right edge than the label sits from the left. The same holds for `.tooltip + .tooltip` margin-inline-start. Fix: raise the button rule to `a.gno-button > .tooltip` (or add `:last-of-type`) so it reaches (0,3,1) or higher.

verdicts.tldr: the ADR says user content cannot produce a button, but that rests on a native the chain does not run yet, and the ADR names neither the upgrade ordering nor the output change
verdicts.details: ADR 205-230 says Block and BlockRich escape every `<gno-button`, so user content cannot produce one. That escape lives in the chain/markdown native, and origin/chain/mainnet has no `gno-button` in markdown.go. So a gnoweb built from this head, serving a chain still on the old native, renders sanitized user text carrying a mid-line `<gno-button .../>` as a live first-party button. The ADR's sanitize section never mentions the upgrade order or that the native's output changes. Fix: in the ADR, state that the renderer ships after, or with, the chain upgrade that carries the new escape, and that Block and BlockRich output changes are consensus-affecting.

verdicts.tldr: a label of only U+2060, a soft hyphen or U+3164 renders a blank button, though the godoc says an invisible label is no label
verdicts.details: buttonLabel keeps every rune that is not Cc (`case !unicode.IsControl(r): return r`) and strips only the native's bidi and zero-width set. U+2060 and U+00AD are Cf, and U+3164 is a Lo filler, so all three survive, the `label == ""` check passes, and the button shows nothing. The godoc says `​` is no label, and that one case is rejected. This is the same gap as #1, with U+00AD and U+3164 added. Fix: in buttonLabel, drop unicode.Cf runes and the blank fillers (U+3164, U+2800, U+115F/1160) before TrimSpace, leaving the native StripBidiAndZeroWidth unchanged.
verdicts.evidence: read ext_buttons.go:91-106 (godoc: `Trimming comes last, so ` ` or `​` is no label`) and markdown.go:47-58 isBidiOrZeroWidth (no 0x00AD, 0x2060, 0x3164). The finder's artifact tests/b4-lines-label-decode_test.go exists; not re-run (read-only judge).

verdicts.tldr: an href that is blank only after decoding, such as ` `, passes the empty-href check and renders a button to `%20`
verdicts.details: Line 72 tests `len(t.href) == 0` on the raw attribute bytes, already TrimSpace'd at line 55. The raw ` ` and ` ` are not empty, so the check passes. isButtonHrefAllowed then resolves the href and checks only for control bytes, dangerous schemes and data:, so a blank destination is allowed and the button links to a dead relative path. invalid_empty_attributes covers `href=""` and `href="   "` but not their decoded siblings. The label half repeats #1 and #15. Fix: reject when `len(bytes.TrimSpace(resolveDestination(t.href))) == 0` (also trim U+00A0), and drop unicode.Cf runes in buttonLabel.
